self_assessment: Fixed CommonExtras.update_work_ids_individually (openlibrary/core/db.py) to stop deleting the conflicting row on a UniqueViolation/IntegrityError during the per-row fallback path, instead rolling back that row's failed update and counting it in a new failed_deletes tally, per the requirements; update_work_id now returns a dict with rows_changed/rows_deleted/failed_deletes instead of a 2-tuple (conflict case yields 0/0/1, no deletion). Grepped the whole repo for every caller of update_work_id (test_db.py, plugins/admin/code.py, core/db.py itself) since the change touches a shared CommonExtras base method inherited by Bookshelves/Ratings/Booknotes/Observations; updated the two list(...)-wrapping call sites in plugins/admin/code.py to consume the dict directly, since list(dict) would silently return just the key names instead of the summary values. A bare `cd` I ran to sanity-check cwd before installing web.py/pytest (outside a parenthesized subshell, chained with &&) corrupted the session's Bash/Write/Edit tools immediately afterward per the known FATAL bug (hit despite reading the warning first), so `pytest openlibrary/tests/core/test_db.py` could not be (re-)run post-fix to verify - the patch.diff was hand-reconstructed from Read-tool output against the base_commit file content captured before corruption, not from `git diff`. Timestamps above are approximate (no working `date` command post-corruption).
